prompt:
Repaint the FIRST IMAGE as a unified medieval town pixel-art concept, keeping its EXACT geometry, proportions and street edges. First image is a locked 40x30-cell construction layout, 48 pixels per cell; aqua grid lines are guide marks that MUST DISAPPEAR in your painting. The second image is style/depth inspiration ONLY, do not copy its plan or oversized landmarks. Keep the first image's 9 dense perimeter blocks with buildings on all four sides and complete attached pitched rear roofs; tiny purposeful courts. Keep every FIRST-IMAGE street boundary and all landmark footprints EXACTLY: main road 2 cells (96 native px), side streets 1 cell (48px), hard orthogonal dogleg beside the gate, no chamfers, no rounded kerbs. Church WEST of the square, guildhall NORTH, west-facing inn EAST, fully roofed north-open market SOUTH; connected low shops frame the market on both sides. South gate stays at the first image's location and width as ONE chamber/landing assembly. Towers only on the wall line. First image already has the desired road and clearances. Unify the roofs into the second image's coherent, deep attached pitched volumes and valleys without shifting building feet or changing storey counts. Keep first image's slate in east blocks, terracotta west/civic, chocolate BROWN in southern peripheral blocks. Use fantasy-house reference high 3/4 projection, exact square pixel clusters, 1 native pixel contours, broad top-left light, 6-8 native pixel shingle clusters and 3-4px row spacing, quiet paving. Make no procedural texture or soft/dither speckle. No labels/grid. Whole district, same framing as first image, exterior solid magenta. This is a meticulous paintover of FIRST IMAGE; preserve its geometric street mask and the size of the guildhall/church/market/gate. Large landscape 4:3 output.
Alternative A: Use more paired, alternating front gables within the SAME building feet. Keep quiet narrow roof ridges connecting same-height terrace neighbours.
role: Final fixed-layout guide; not enlarged as the deliverable
